title: Steady on Her Feet?

patient.name: Mdm Wong Siok Tin
patient.presenting_complaint: Came in for routine cataract review and has just had both eyes dilated — now waiting to be seen, vision very blurry

history.hpc: Mdm Wong is an 81-year-old attending for cataract assessment. Both eyes were dilated with tropicamide 1% about 20 minutes ago and her vision is now very blurry, especially for near objects, and she is sensitive to the bright clinic lights. She mentions she had a small fall at home about 2 months ago when she tripped over a rug, but did not injure herself badly. She uses a walking stick occasionally but did not bring it today. She came with her domestic helper but the helper has gone to the toilet.
history.pmhx: Bilateral cataracts (moderate). Osteoporosis. Hypertension. History of one fall at home 2 months ago (no fracture).
medications: Calcium and Vitamin D supplement OD
history.social_hx: Lives with domestic helper and son's family. Uses a walking stick occasionally. Today the helper has briefly stepped away.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Bilateral moderate nuclear cataracts. Pupils now well-dilated bilaterally following tropicamide instillation.
examination_findings.fundus: To be assessed by doctor now that pupils are dilated

investigations.fall_risk_assessment: High risk identified: age >80, recent fall history within past 3 months, osteoporosis, reduced baseline vision further worsened by pupil dilation, walking aid not available today, and currently unaccompanied
investigations.va_distance: RE: LogMAR 0.5 (6/18). LE: LogMAR 0.6 (6/24). Measured pre-dilation.

diagnosis: High fall risk — elderly patient with recent fall history, reduced baseline vision, and acute post-dilation blurring/photosensitivity, currently without her walking aid and temporarily unaccompanied. Requires active fall-prevention measures while waiting.

immediate: Recognise that ALL patients should be assessed for fall risk at every visit, and that this patient has multiple risk factors
Do not leave the patient to walk to the waiting area alone — accompany her personally
Seat her in a safe, well-lit area close to the nursing/OA station where she can be observed
Offer sunglasses/UV protectors to reduce photosensitivity discomfort while dilated
Locate her domestic helper or ask staff to find the helper and ask them to remain with the patient
Document the fall risk assessment and the actions taken (e.g. accompanied to seating, helper informed, sunglasses offered)
Inform the nurse-in-charge that this patient is high fall risk and post-dilation, so staff are aware when calling her for the next step
follow_up: Doctor to proceed with dilated fundus examination for cataract assessment
Ensure patient is escorted by helper/family for the rest of the visit and on the way out
Consider flagging in her records that she should bring her walking stick to future visits, especially for appointments involving dilation
patient_education: Explain to Mdm Wong that her vision will be blurry and she will be more sensitive to light for the next 4-6 hours due to the dilating drops
Advise her to move slowly, hold onto rails/furniture, and not to walk around alone until her helper returns
Advise her to bring her walking stick and a companion for future visits, especially when dilation is expected
Reassure her that this blurring is temporary and expected after dilation

key_points: Asks about recent falls and any walking aids normally used
Asks about who accompanied the patient and whether they are currently present
Notes baseline vision and relevant comorbidities (osteoporosis, hypertension)
Recognises post-dilation blurring and photosensitivity as additional acute risk factors
Performs/documents a fall risk assessment for this patient at this visit
Identifies multiple specific risk factors (age, recent fall, osteoporosis, reduced VA, post-dilation blurring, no walking aid, currently unaccompanied)
Considers the timing of dilation relative to current symptoms
Documents pre-dilation VA and IOP appropriately
Correctly classifies this patient as high fall risk
Recognises that dilation has acutely increased her fall risk on top of existing chronic risk factors
Understands that 'high risk' requires an active response, not just documentation
Does not dismiss the risk because the patient 'seems fine sitting down'
Takes concrete action: accompanies patient, seats her safely, locates helper/family
Offers practical measures (sunglasses/UV protectors) for post-dilation photosensitivity
Documents the fall risk assessment and actions taken, as required
Communicates the fall risk status to other staff (nurse-in-charge)
Provides clear patient education about post-dilation effects and safety
